report:
Reviewed all four implementation entries and both associated tests against the complete claim. Requirements are (1) retain represented alternatives, (2) represent source exhaustiveness independently, and (3) permit a definitive absent-name/provider conclusion only for exhaustive empty results; incomplete empty results must remain uncertainty. The linked architectural rationale distinguishes terminal incompleteness from logical negative evidence.

This remains a partially implemented, explicitly deferred contract. The semantic_spec TODO implementation accurately states that uniform completeness across all lookup forms is absent: resolve_path and resolve_name_from_scope still return Vec<Resolution>, and ordinary module/path lookup returns vectors without a completeness component. No approval of those APIs as satisfying the full contract is implied. Its TODO test explicitly lists absent, unique, ambiguous, incomplete, and incomplete-empty provider cases and the exhaustive-empty negative boundary. Implementing the uniform result and propagating it through ordinary lookup consumers is the prerequisite for that full matrix. The placeholder has no assertions and is not behavioral evidence; retaining this existing TODO is justified.

The three ordinary implementation associations capture the existing method-provider slice. Resolver::traits_in_method_scope returns distinct trait identities plus a separate complete boolean; it retains enumerated providers while unresolved imports, local glob limitations, unavailable/ambiguous prelude routes, and module expansion hazards make the search incomplete. local_syms/mods.rs computes method-provider expansion completeness separately from the expanded item list. In the exercised unresolved bang-macro case, resolve_bang_macro has no unique macro identity, bang_macro_expansion_complete returns false, and module_expansion_complete returns false. check/method.rs initializes unknown from that boolean and other provider limitations, accumulates represented definite candidates, selects a unique candidate only without unknown, and emits incomplete candidate information instead of no applicable method when unknown is set. These associations establish that partial route, not an exhaustive implementation of every lookup form. Other limitations in the supplied files remain within the explicit broad TODO.

The ordinary unresolved_item_macro_keeps_method_scope_incomplete test builds Rust source containing unknown_items!(), a derived Clone implementation, and a method calling self.db.clone(). It forces the real expanded-module and function-body queries and visibly asserts an incomplete-candidate diagnostic. Captured setup helpers create the source-backed root module and parse it; captured BuiltinDeriveTcx supplies synthetic std/core metadata, so this is a focused provider-boundary regression rather than an independent rustc-backed end-to-end compatibility proof. Its assertion would detect replacing that uncertainty diagnostic with only a definitive no-method diagnostic. It does not establish the complete absent/unique/ambiguous/empty-incomplete matrix, retention of every alternative, or a complete negative result: those remain covered by the explicit TODO rather than being inferred from this passing test.

Added only implementation association comments in check/method.rs, check/resolve/mod.rs, and local_syms/mods.rs, then restarted and reviewed the fresh captured inputs. Captured test helpers and relevant review/specification context with review read. Executed cargo fmt and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib derive_expansion_tests::unresolved_item_macro_keeps_method_scope_incomplete -- --exact: one test passed. Workspace cargo build was also launched; build completion is reported separately by the coordinator. Source assessment and the focused executed test are distinct evidence. Central delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks are coordinated by root for these comment-only edits. No additional edits are requested; the broader contract and matrix remain visibly TODO.
